target: Bracts (involucre, bract PO:0009055) are absent (PATO:0000462) and that statement stands. 'subulate or linear' describes the bracteoles of the umbellets: bracteole PO:0009043, subulate PATO:0001954
fix: In Apiaceae, 'bracts' means the involucre of the umbel and 'bracteoles' means the involucel of the umbellets. A shape that follows 'bracteoles' maps to bracteole PO:0009043 and never falls back to bract PO:0009055. 'bracteole' must not resolve to bract through the PO synonym list.

target: Nothing is absent and no flower annotation should be made. Male flowers (staminate flower PO:0025600) were not collected. The umbel (PO:0030129) statement stands
fix: '<part> not seen', 'not known', 'unknown' and 'not yet collected' report a gap in the material. They are never an absence (PATO:0000462). Drop them. A sex word ('male flowers', 'female flowers') must also never fall back to flower PO:0009046.

target: Only the submarginal (intramarginal) vein is absent: leaf lamina vein PO:0020138 absent (PATO:0000462), context 'submarginal'. 'ending in punctate teeth' describes where the lateral veins end at the leaf lamina margin (PO:0025009) and is not a vein quality

target: Nothing is absent. 'not seen' is a gap in the material, probably because the stipules fall early. Keep stipule PO:0020041 caducous and drop the absence
fix: A bare 'not seen' never yields an absence (PATO:0000462). Also, 'caducous' or 'early deciduous' followed by 'not seen' means the part fell off before collection.

target: Nothing is absent: the inflorescences and flowers were not collected. 'Infructescences cymose-paniculate' belongs to infructescence PO:0006342, not to inflorescence
fix: 'Inflorescences and flowers not seen' reports a gap in the material and is never an absence. 'Infructescence(s)' maps to infructescence PO:0006342 and never falls back to inflorescence PO:0009049.
reason: Only fruiting material was seen. The infructescence proves the plant has inflorescences.

target: Nothing is absent: the inflorescences and flowers were not collected. 'Infructescences terminal' belongs to infructescence PO:0006342, with a terminal position
fix: 'Inflorescences and flowers not seen' is a gap in the material and is never an absence. 'Infructescence' maps to infructescence PO:0006342, not to inflorescence PO:0009049.
reason: Only fruiting specimens were seen.

target: Only small prickles and bristles are absent: prickle PO:0025169 with context 'small', and bristles (trichome PO:0000282), absent (PATO:0000462). The large prickles are present and often paired or opposite. Both statements should use prickle PO:0025169, not thorn PO:0025172
fix: 'small prickles and bristles absent', 'without acicles' and 'without glandular bristles' in Rosa deny one kind of armature. Keep the size or kind as the context. In Rosa, 'prickle(s)' maps to prickle PO:0025169 (an outgrowth of the epidermis) and never to thorn PO:0025172 (a modified shoot).
reason: Rosa xanthina has stout prickles, often paired below the leaves, and lacks the fine prickles and bristles. 'Thorn' is botanically wrong for a rose.

target: The stem (PO:0009047) is absent (an acaulescent cushion plant). 'much branched' describes the rhizome or caudex (rhizome PO:0004542), branched
fix: In a stemless (acaulescent) taxon, 'much branched' or 'branched' in the stock or rhizome sentence maps to rhizome PO:0004542. It should never take stem as the subject by default when 'stemless' is stated in the same description.
reason: Saussurea wernerioides is a stemless cushion plant whose branched rootstock forms the cushion.

target: Only sterile (non-flowering) stems are absent: stem PO:0009047 with context 'sterile', absent (PATO:0000462). The flowering stems are present, erect and branched from the base
fix: 'sterile stems absent' and 'non-flowering shoots absent' (Crassulaceae) deny one kind of shoot. Keep 'sterile' or 'flowering' as the context and never record 'stem absent'.
reason: In Sedum the description separates flowering from sterile stems. This species has only flowering stems.

target: Only bisexual inflorescences are absent: inflorescence PO:0009049 with context 'bisexual', absent (PATO:0000462). 'Male inflorescences axillary' belongs to staminate inflorescence PO:0025601
fix: 'bisexual inflorescences absent', 'androgynous inflorescences absent' and 'male inflorescences ...' carry a sex qualifier. Keep it as the context or the specific PO class (staminate inflorescence PO:0025601), and never record 'inflorescence absent'.
reason: Streblus taxoides is dioecious, with unisexual inflorescences only.

target: The flowering stems (stem PO:0009047) are leafless except at one end. The leaves (PO:0025034) are crowded in a rosette there. Keep the stretch of stem as the context
fix: 'leafless except at apex/base', 'leafless below' and 'leafless above' give where the leaves sit on the stem. Keep the position as the context and never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: The two statements are about different stretches of the same stem.

target: The capitulum is ecalyculate: calyculus bracts (bracteole PO:0009043, context 'calyculus') absent (PATO:0000462). 'herbaceous' describes the phyllaries (involucral bract PO:0009045)
fix: In Asteraceae, 'not bracteolate', 'ecalyculate' and 'calyculus absent' deny only the outer calyculus bracts of the capitulum. Never record 'bract absent'. Phyllaries map to involucral bract PO:0009045.
reason: Tephroseris has an involucre of herbaceous phyllaries and usually no calyculus.

target: Only ray florets are absent: ray flower PO:0025331 absent (PATO:0000462). The disc florets are present. 'Capitula solitary, terminal' belongs to capitulum inflorescence PO:0030121
fix: 'ray florets absent', 'rays absent' and 'capitula discoid' map to ray flower PO:0025331 and never fall back to flower PO:0009046.
reason: Tripleurospermum homogamum is discoid (hence the name): its capitula have only disc florets.

target: 'not always present' means sometimes absent. The bract it refers to is a different whorl (probably the inner or receptacular bracts) from the leaflike outer involucral bracts (PO:0009045)
fix: 'not always present', 'sometimes absent', 'occasionally absent' and 'absent or present' describe variation. They are never an absence (PATO:0000462). Record them as variable presence or drop them.
reason: A part that is sometimes present cannot contradict a description of the same part. The outer bracts are certainly there.

target: Only the septum of the fruit lacks a vein: fruit septum PO:0025268, vein (vascular bundle PO:0005020) absent. 'veined' probably describes the valves (fruit valve PO:0000033)
fix: 'septum not veined' and 'septum nerveless' (Brassicaceae fruits) are a quality of fruit septum PO:0025268. They are never a taxon-wide 'vascular bundle absent'. Keep the part that is not veined as the bearer.
reason: Brassicaceae fruits often have veined valves and a veinless septum. The two statements are about different parts.

target: A named part (probably the fruit septum PO:0025268 or the beak) is not veined. The 'prominent mid-vein' belongs to the fruit valve PO:0000033, or to the leaf midvein PO:0020139 if it is leaf text
fix: A bare 'not veined' or 'nerveless' takes the part of the preceding clause as its bearer. It is never 'vascular bundle absent'. 'mid-vein' or 'midrib' maps to leaf midvein PO:0020139 or a valve vein, not to vascular bundle in general.
reason: The plant cannot be without vascular bundles. The two statements are about different organs.

target: Only the basal leaf is absent: leaf PO:0025034 with context 'basal', absent. The narrowly lanceolate leaves are the cauline leaves (cauline leaf PO:0000013)
fix: 'without basal leaf', 'basal leaves absent' and 'basal leaves withered at anthesis' deny one position of leaf. Keep 'basal' as the context, and give the stage if one is stated. Never record 'leaf absent'.
reason: The stem leaves are described, so the plant is not leafless.

target: The stem (PO:0009047) is leafless only on its lower part. The cauline leaves (PO:0000013), which are opposite, sit higher up
fix: 'stem leafless below' and 'leafless in lower part' describe where on the stem the leaves sit. Keep the position as the context and never record 'leaf absent'.
reason: The two statements are about different stretches of the stem.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) is usually absent ('generally'). The leaves that occur on young shoots are small and thick. Keep 'generally' (usually absent) as the context
fix: 'generally leafless', 'usually leafless', 'often leafless' and 'leafless or nearly so' give a frequency. They are never a plain absence (PATO:0000462). Record them as usually absent, or drop the absence when the leaves are also described.
reason: Periploca aphylla is functionally leafless, but small, early-falling leaves occur on young growth.

target: Only the leaves that subtend the flower whorls are absent: the inflorescence (PO:0009049) whorls are without subtending leaves (bract PO:0009055 or leaf with context 'subtending the whorls', absent). The stem and basal leaves are present
fix: 'without subtending leaves', 'ebracteate whorls' and 'verticels leafless' (Polygonaceae) are about the inflorescence. Never record 'leaf absent'.

target: Nothing is absent and no leaf annotation should be made. 'Specialized asexual reproduction not seen' means no gemmae or brood bodies (gemma PO:0025614) were observed
fix: 'specialized asexual reproduction not seen', 'absent' or 'unknown' (moss floras) is about gemmae, brood bodies or deciduous leaves. It is never 'leaf absent'. With 'not seen', drop it.
reason: The sentence is about how the plant reproduces, not about its leaves, which are described as straight.

target: Only the limbidium is lacking: limbidium FLOPO:0986075 absent (PATO:0000462) on most leaves, keeping 'most leaves' as the context
fix: In Fissidens, 'limbidia not differentiated', 'limbidium absent' and 'unbordered' map to limbidium FLOPO:0986075. They are never 'leaf absent'.
reason: The limbidium is a border on the leaf. The leaves themselves are present and lanceolate.

target: Only bracts below the glumes are absent: bract PO:0009055 with context 'subtending the spikelet', absent. The lemma (PO:0009037) is a separate bract within the spikelet and is mucronate
fix: 'without bracts below the glumes' and 'spikelets not subtended by bracts' (bamboos) deny only bracts outside the spikelet (PO:0009051). Keep that position as the context. Never record a general 'bract absent', which also denies glumes, lemmas and paleas.
reason: Grasses always have glumes and lemmas. The absence is about extra bracts on the inflorescence branches.

target: Only the terminal spine of the costa is absent: leaf midvein (costa) PO:0020139 with context 'terminal spine', absent. The leaves and their margins are present
fix: 'terminal spine absent', 'costa ending without a spine' and 'apex without a spine' (mosses) describe the end of the costa or the leaf apex (PO:0020137). They are never 'leaf absent'.

target: The capsule is absent only in northern hemisphere specimens, so keep 'northern hemisphere material' as the context. In a moss the capsule is sporangium PO:0025094, not capsule fruit PO:0030091, for both statements
fix: 'absent in <region> material', 'not known in <region>' and 'sporophytes unknown in <region>' limit an absence to one region or set of specimens. Keep the region as the context. In moss floras, 'capsule' maps to sporangium PO:0025094.
reason: Sporophytes are known from elsewhere and are described there.

target: Nothing is absent. The distal leaves are present and do not fall off (they are not deciduous). Drop the absence. At most, record the distal leaves as persistent
fix: 'without deciduous <part>' and 'lacking caducous <part>' deny a quality (falling off), not the part. Never record the part as absent.
reason: This is a key statement contrasting with species that shed their distal leaves as propagules. The leaves are described.

target: Only the stipels are absent: stipel PO:0020051 absent (PATO:0000462). The stipules (PO:0020041) are present and small
fix: French 'stipelle(s)' and English 'stipel(s)' map to stipel PO:0020051 and never to stipule PO:0020041.

target: 'parfois absentes' (sometimes absent) refers to one kind of floret, probably the marginal female florets (pistillate flower PO:0025599). The capitulum (PO:0030121) is campanulate
fix: French 'parfois absent(e)s', 'quelquefois absent(e)s' and 'souvent absent(e)s' express variation. They are never an absence (PATO:0000462). The noun they refer to comes from the preceding clause, and is often a qualified floret, never 'flower' in general.

target: Only the stipels are absent: stipel PO:0020051 absent (PATO:0000462). The stipules (PO:0020041) are present and very caducous
fix: 'sans stipelles' and 'stipelles absentes' map to stipel PO:0020051, never to stipule PO:0020041.

target: 'parfois absentes' (sometimes absent) refers to the bracteoles (PO:0009043), probably. The bracts (PO:0009055) are present and ciliate
fix: French 'parfois absentes' is variation and never a plain absence. Find the noun it refers to in the preceding clause. Keep 'bractéoles' at bracteole PO:0009043, without falling back to bract.
